items.title: Asian Stocks Steady as Traders Await Fed Decision: Markets Wrap
items.content: Asian stocks were broadly steady as elevated oil prices and rising bond yields kept investors cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.

items.title: Shrinking Chinese Fuel Inventories Raise Chance of Export Curbs
items.content: China’s gasoline and diesel inventories are plunging as refiners grapple with a tightening domestic market, raising the chance the government may move to limit fuel exports again.

items.title: Japan’s Export Growth Stays Solid as Shipments of Chips Jump
items.content: Japan’s export growth slowed a tad in August while remaining at an elevated pace, with shipments of semiconductors and chips manufacturing equipment surging.

items.title: Gold Steadies Below $4,300 as Markets Await Fed Rate Decision
items.content: Gold was steady as high oil prices continued to fuel inflation concerns and keep interest-rate hike bets a near-certainty ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision later Wednesday.

items.content: Apollo Global Management has provided $585 million of financing to flexible workspace provider The Executive Centre, according to a statement, in the global asset manager’s largest Asian hybrid deal combining debt and equity.

items.title: Thai Finance Chief Sticks to 2.5% Growth Goal
items.content: Thai Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas is sticking with the government’s forecast for 2.5% economic growth this year despite the surge in oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Fed Seen Hiking Rates in Defiance of Trump: Decision-Day Guide
items.content: The Federal Reserve is expected to lift interest rates on Wednesday for the first time since 2023 as policymakers lose confidence that inflation will cool sufficiently without at least a nudge from the central bank.

items.title: Retirement Math Difficult for Investors, says BlackRock's Magyera
items.content: Jaime Magyera, BlackRock senior managing director and head of US Wealth and head of Retirement, said advisers are using artificial intelligence to help parse increasingly complex capital markets after AI company Anthropic announces new ties with Blackrock. Magyera also said that AI is helping create more strategic customization for clients. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Market Attractive But Issues Lurk, Oaktree's Poli Says
items.content: Oaktree Portfolio Manager Danielle Poli says markets may continue to see upward pressure on yields because investors do not yet believe inflation will be fully tamed. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Dutch Bros CEO Christine Barone on Expansion & Inflation
items.content: Christine Barone, President & CEO of Dutch Bros, discussed the company’s aggressive growth strategy, saying the chain aims to reach 2,029 shops by 2029 and expects to add at least 185 locations this year. She said that pace is supported by a strong internal talent pipeline, with more than 500 operators ready to move into new states and markets as the company expands. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Wealthy Clients Want 'Shiny Star' Investments, Says Rick Pitcairn
items.content: Rick Pitcairn, chairman and chief global strategist at family office Pitcairn, said its his job to tap the breaks on wealthy clients who want to put too much of their money in 'shiny star' investments like SpaceX or private markets. Pitcairn said that there is a role for private credit and private markets, but it should be inside a diverse portfolio.  (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007 as Fed Looms
items.content: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose to the highest in almost two decades, the latest milestone in a bruising global bond selloff driven by booming capital investment and soaring energy prices that are exacerbating inflation.

items.content: Bond traders have piled into bearish positions ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, betting that the Treasury selloff driving yields to their highest levels in almost two decades will continue.

items.title: Gold Isn't Driven by US Inflation Says Jan van Eck
items.content: Jan van Eck, CEO of VanEck Funds joined Bloomberg Businessweek Daily from Future Proof to discuss the state of the global economy. He says he isn't worried about the $40 Trillion US debt and that Bessent and Trump are 'toying' with the market when it comes to the idea of sending $5,000 checks to Americans if they keep control of Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)
